themes_detail.label: Sudden Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 148 THIS WEEK—a 469% jump from the 26-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting rapid pavement or infrastructure failure across CD 402 requiring immediate DOT inspection.
evidence: 148 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 26.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 11.89)
469% spike over 8-week average indicates acute, localized deterioration event
Correlates with simultaneous spike in street sweeping complaints (5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 avg), suggesting debris or damage accumulation
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: Which streets are worst affected? Walk the district and photograph conditions.
DOT accountability: Why wasn't preventive maintenance catching this? Interview department about response timeline.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 3900% spike—indicating a coordinated advertising or graffiti campaign now underway in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 14.74)
3900% spike concentration in single week suggests coordinated campaign, not organic litter
Paired with spike in 'outside building' complaints (3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 avg), indicating exterior/facade targeting
reporting_angles: Visual survey: Map where illegal postings are concentrated (storefronts, residential, transit hubs?) and photograph.
Pattern analysis: Is this political campaign material, nightlife venue promotions, or something else? Interview 311 data or local precinct.

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures Surge
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints reached 168 LAST WEEK—a 285% increase from the 43.6-complaint weekly average—creating potential public safety hazards and commute delays across the district.
evidence: 168 traffic signal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 43.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.03)
285% spike over 8-week average indicates systemwide signal failure, not isolated incidents
High public safety implications: malfunctioning signals create collision risk and pedestrian danger
reporting_angles: Safety impact: Interview residents and commuters about near-misses or accidents at problem intersections; request NYPD collision data.
DOT accountability: Which signals failed and why? Request DOT maintenance records and timeline for repairs.

themes_detail.label: Damaged Tree Surge Following Weather Event
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints peaked at 33 two weeks ago—a 1367% spike from the 2.2-complaint weekly baseline—suggesting storm damage or pest infestation now requiring Parks Department triage and removal.
evidence: 33 damaged tree complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.2 weekly average (z-score: 17.94)
1367% spike is highest z-score in dataset, indicating acute weather or pest event
Likely tied to recent storm activity (check weather data from 2 weeks prior to spike)
reporting_angles: Environmental aftermath: Did a specific storm cause this? Map which streets have downed/damaged trees and verify Parks response.
Parks maintenance: What's the backlog for tree removal? How long are residents waiting for responses?

themes_detail.label: Animal Nuisance & Building Exterior Issues
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about unsanitary animal conditions on private property and 'outside building' issues both spiked to 3 THIS WEEK from negligible baselines (0.1 avg each)—a 2300% jump each—potentially indicating a pest infestation or rodent colony.
evidence: 3 unsanitary animal private property complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 baseline (z-score: 8.69)
3 outside building complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 baseline (z-score: 8.69), same spike timing
Dual spike suggests single source: rodent colony, feral animal den, or neglected animal care on single or adjacent properties
reporting_angles: Source investigation: Which address(es) are generating these complaints? Follow up with building owners and health dept.
Public health angle: What health risks do residents face? Interview Health Dept. on outbreak risk or disease vectors.
